prerequisites: Writing algorithms in the form of flowcharts or block diagrams

learning_outcomes.text: In-depth knowledge and understanding of the fundamental theoretical and applicative aspects of the LabVIEW development environment.
Ability to set up the design and management of even complex measurement systems.
Ability to correctly interpret the results provided by a measurement system.
Ability to communicate information both orally and in writing with the right level of detail.
Ability to discuss problems and solutions with specialist and non-specialist interlocutors.
Ability to continuously learn, through the correct interpretation of technical bibliography and manufacturers' manuals.
Able to create applications, based on design models or customized, to acquire, process, analyze, visualize and archive real-world data.

syllabus_topics: The front panel and the block diagram
Programming methods with different Design Patterns
Methods for saving data to files and displaying saved data
Programming practices for code reuse and readability
Development of a distributed measurement architecture
Stand alone and modular instrumentation (systems based on low-cost devices, multifunction data acquisition cards, cRIO and LXI systems)
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral exam. The exam score is awarded through a grade expressed in thirtieths, averaged between the written and oral, with a positive evaluation starting from the grade of 18/30. To achieve a score of 30/30 with honors, the student must demonstrate excellent knowledge of the topics discussed. The exam also evaluates the possibility of accessing the NI CLAD exam.
